subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.

spec.name: Longbow-6 Railgun Carrier
spec.description: A six-wheeled low-poly sci-fi military railgun carrier with a long twin-rail cannon on a turret, braced on four hydraulic stabiliser legs.
spec.layout: Long heavy truck-like vehicle facing +Z. Front: angular armoured cab (cab sits z 2.6..4.3) with sloped glacis, slit windscreen with cyan glow visor, headlamps and a bull-bar. Middle and rear: a flat chassis deck (top y=1.45) carrying a rotating turret ring at z=-0.6 and a railgun whose twin rails run forward over the cab to a muzzle at z=4.8 (raised slightly, about 8 degrees elevation) and back into a breech housing with capacitor banks. Six big chunky wheels in three axles (z=3.2, -0.6, -3.2) at x=+-1.45, radius 0.62, resting on y=0. Four stabiliser legs fold out diagonally at the corners (outriggers at z=1.2 and z=-3.9, extending to x=+-1.75 footpads at y=0 with flat pads) braced down, slightly lifting nothing visibly. Style: blocky faceted low-poly armour plates, chamfered boxes, hazard-yellow stripe trim, panelled paints with rivets, cyan neon accents on rails, capacitors and visor (glow kit), dark gunmetal rails. Every part uses flat shading and a few decal textures: unit emblem, stencil numbers, hazard chevrons.

parts.builds: Main frame and deck between cab and tail: a chamfered box girder underbody (y 0.75..1.45), side skirts with panelled rivet paint in hull colours, wheel arches cut as dark recessed boxes over the three axles, rear bumper with tow hooks and tail lights (warnRed, glow), hazard-yellow chevron strips along the deck edges and rear, deck plating with hatch plates and cable conduits, turret-ring base (lathe collar, gunmetal, with ring teeth) at turretRing, fuel and equipment lockers on the sides, stencil numbers and unit emblem textures on flanks, and mounting stubs where the stabiliser legs attach at stabFL/FR/RL/RR (boxy sockets).
parts.attaches: Cab starts at cabRear (z=2.4). Turret rides on turretRing. Wheels hang at axleF/M/R; stabiliser sockets at stab* mounts.

parts.builds: Armoured front cab and nose from z=2.4 to 4.5: faceted sloped-glacis hull, angular roof with sensor mast and antenna, a slit windscreen with glassDark glass and neonCyan glowing visor strip, side vision ports, armoured door panels with handle and hazard stripes, headlamps (glow white), bull-bar/ram bumper with hazard chevrons, mirrors, roof light bar, exhaust stacks behind the cab, tow shackles, unit decal on the door. Panelled paint with rivets and subtle wear paint (darker low, lighter top). The cab roof is at about y=2.5 and the gun passes above it.
parts.attaches: Rear face sits on cabRear against the chassis front. Front wheels' arches at axleF are cut into its lower sides.

parts.builds: Six chunky low-poly wheels (radius 0.62, width 0.5): rubber tyres as 10-sided lathes with tread blocks ringed around, steel rim discs with bolt rings and a hub cap with a stencil textured disc, one wheel part per wheel on its wheel joint; axles/differential housings (gunmetal cylinders) and leaf-spring/suspension arms from each axle line to the chassis, plus mud flaps and mudguard fenders in hull colour with hazard edge, front-axle steering linkage. Wheels sit at x=+-1.45 at the three axle mounts, lowest points at y=0.
parts.attaches: Wheel centres at axleF/axleM/axleR height 0.62, x=+-1.45; suspension arms reach in to the chassis girder at x=+-0.9.

parts.builds: Four deployed hydraulic outrigger legs: at each stab* mount a boxy hinge bracket with pin, a pivoting upper arm (frustumBox) sloping outward and down, a telescoping piston cylinder (steel/hydraulic colour, two stages) angled down to a wide octagonal footpad with ribbed underside resting flat on y=0 at x=+-1.9..+-2.0 (front z~1.2, rear z~-3.9), diagonal brace strut, hazard-yellow banding on the piston outer sleeve, warning red caution decals, hoses (thin sweeps) linking to the chassis, and small cyan status lights. Left and right mirrored. Footpads are the floor contact.
parts.attaches: Upper ends at stabFL/FR/RL/RR mounts on the chassis sockets; each leg rides its own stab joint.

parts.builds: Rotating turret and the railgun. Turret on the turretRing: low faceted armoured housing (y 1.45..2.9, z -2.2..0.9) with sloped panels, crew hatch, sensor domes, vents, rear breech housing with cyan-glowing capacitor cells in rows (glow), cable bundles, hazard stripes, panelled paint and a roman-numeral/emblem decal on the sides. The railgun on the gun joint at gunPivot, about 8 degrees elevation: two parallel gunmetal slab rails (box section) spaced 0.28 apart running from z=-1.5 to the muzzle at z=4.8 over the cab, with cyan glowing inner edge strips between the rails, insulating spacer blocks and clamp rings every 0.6 m (steel), a heavy recoil sleeve and hydraulic recoil cylinders at the rear, flared muzzle shroud with brake fins and a glowing cyan muzzle ring, elevation trunnion blocks on the turret sides, a bolt-on muzzle sight. The gun joint carries rails, spacers and muzzle; the turret joint carries the housing.
parts.attaches: Turret base sits on turretRing (y=1.45); gun pivots at gunPivot; muzzle ends at the muzzle mount, passing above the cab roof (cab top y<=2.7).

calls.reasoning:
I'm working out the stabiliser function per leg, computing mount positions based on side offsets and attaching parts to their joint bones.

Designing the outrigger geometry now: bracket, upper arm, elbow, and piston placement, plus a diagonal brace strut connecting back to the chassis, with telescoping piston stages using layered cylinders for the sleeve and inner rod.

For the footpad, I'm shaping an octagonal lathe profile with a beveled edge, then checking that its radius keeps it within the bounding box -- settling on a smaller radius around 0.36 so the pad fits without exceeding the chassis limits, and adding ribbed detail on top instead of underneath to avoid clipping the floor.

Now I'm placing the wheels with their radius and width, mirroring positions across the x-axis, and confirming the lathe axis defaults work fine for the frustum box shapes. I'm planning decal details like a warning triangle plate, a glowing status light sphere, a sweeping hose connecting the chassis to the piston, and a hinge pin cylinder.

For the sleeve I'm setting up alternating hazard stripe bands with a color array, falling back to a default color elsewhere, and considering a mottled paint texture for the hull and bracket using the mottle and countershade helpers. I'm also naming the stabilizer joint and defining the hinge pin as a cylinder oriented along the z-axis.

I'm looping through each leg mount point, placing a boxy bracket with a small chamfer and adding rotated rib boxes along the pad for extra structural detail.
